summary: Build: taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean scaffold/GXScaffold/Branched/Galois.lean exits 0 with no output (4 s). The file contains no sorry, admit or axiom. The downstream scaffold/GXScaffold/Branched/GaloisExamples.lean still typechecks against the rebuilt module, with only its own three sorry warnings (l.877, 1159, 1200). #print axioms, run from /tmp so nothing was written in the repo, gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for galois_correspondence_cc, galoisian_semilocal_cc, galoisian_fiber, alternative_countable, dense_orbits, isSLSCInCC_of_locally_linear, isSLSCInCC_compl_faces_of_locallyFinite, isSLSCInCC_of_local_nhds, isQuasiGaloisian_of_isSpreadCompletion, IsQuasiGaloisian.exists_isSpreadCompletion, isSLSCInCC_univ_of_semilocallySimplyConnected, deckOrdEquiv, galois_quotient and branched_covering_group_automorphisms. Paths, which this file imports, now has no real sorry, and every cited result is built: GX.almostTrivialCC_iff and AlmostTrivial.almostTrivialCC (Paths), and maxBranched_basic, maxBranched_isBranchedCovering, maxBranched_universal and maxBranched_lifting (GX.Branched.Universality). Every decl named in REPORT.json resolves (#check over the whole list, no error). There are no name clashes. A clash with GX/ or Paths would fail the import, GaloisExamples imports this module and compiles, and the 127 declared names do not meet the names in SingularII/Unloopable.lean or Basic.lean. Ledger coverage: all 13 \label{} of l.1417-1559 (sec:galoisian_branched aside) are in REPORT.json. ex:following_situations_semi_locally_simply (l.1561) belongs to GaloisExamples. Fidelity: DEC-55 is applied correctly. AlmostTrivialCC (Paths) is the literal definition: the connectedComponentIn of gamma in OmegaSet U x x, a subset of C(I,X) with mathlib's compact-open topology, meets OmegaSet (V cap U) x x for every V in nhds x. IsSLSCAtCC/IsSLSCInCC transcribe l.1451-1454 on it; IsPreconnected V together with x in V gives the paper's connected V. Where the paper's arguments use homotopies the bridge is proved: homotopy implies literal always (IsSLSCIn.isSLSCInCC), and the two forms are equivalent for U open and slsc in an LPC space (isSLSCInCC_iff). That is the exact situation U = Y minus S of prop:Galoisian_semilocal and theo:Galois_cor, whose own hypotheses provide it. DEC-57 is applied correctly. IsQuasiGaloisian (deck-transitive restriction over some portly O inside ord(Y)) is proved equivalent in both directions to 'the completion of a deck-transitive connected surjective covering of a portly O'; the extra instances on the completion direction (X LPC, Y LPC, Y first countable) are the l.810 standing hypotheses. galoisian_fiber uses IsCNbhd (open, preconnected) and gives a homeomorphism onto the full projective limit GaloisThread, with the product-of-discrete topology. In rem:simple_cases, the locally-flat hypothesis of isSLSCInCC_of_locally_linear (a chart V homeomorphic to E with V inside U, or V minus U equal to the preimage of a closed proper linear subspace) is satisfied by every locally flat submanifold of an R^n-manifold (U open, so X minus U is closed). The simplicial case uses mathlib's Geometry.SimplicialComplex, closed faces and U dense. Satisfiability probes typecheck: IsSLSCInCC univ on R and IsSLSCInCC of the complement of the zero submodule in R x R. maxBranched_isQuasiGaloisian shows IsQuasiGaloisian is inhabited. No hypothesis carries a conclusion. Every weakening is real and reported: no codimension condition, a single neighbourhood rather than a basis in the second item, and no second countability for (ii) => (i) or for theo:Galois_cor. Marks: the 11 marked labels in the first 4000 characters are exactly the rows REPORT.json calls closed. rem:definition_semi_locally_simply_connected and theo:Galois_cor are unmarked and partial, correctly. No ruling accepts either correction: grep of registers/DECISIONS.md finds none, and the ledger lists both as partial. The two partial rows are honest. The converse of l.1455-1457 is false: the harmonic archipelago is a Peano continuum, locally contractible off its base point and not homotopically Hausdorff at it, so every loop is homotopic into every neighbourhood and is almost trivial in both forms, while it is not slsc. For the same reason theo:Galois_cor, which omits 'Y minus S slsc', cannot be read as stated: with S empty and Y the harmonic archipelago the maximal covering does not exist. The added hypothesis is the one prop:universality needs. The theorem is otherwise at least as strong as the paper: normality iff Galoisian holds for every H with H\Y~^S homeomorphic to X over Y, and X lies in an independent universe. The issues below are all minor.

issues.problem: Local finiteness is asked of the faces in the ambient E (LocallyFinite in E), which is strictly stronger than local finiteness at the points of |K|. Example: the segments [1/(n+1), 1/n] of R form a complex locally finite at every point of |K| = (0,1] but not at 0 in E. The proof only uses that B, the union of the faces not containing x, misses a ball around x within |K|, and that follows from local finiteness at the points of |K|. Under DEC-57's 'locally finite geometric complex' the E-reading is defensible, and it is disclosed in the docstring ('closed faces locally finite in E'), but not in the REPORT hypothesis note.
